VIII. ALTERNATIVES TO THE ACTION
Alternative 1: The proposed legislation provides for recognition of two groups of endangered species known as (1) threatened with extinction and (2) likely within the forseeable future to become threatened with 'extinction. Species in the first group are not allowed to be imported into or taken within the U.S. (with certain specified exceptions), but for the second group, the Secretary of the Interior may determine what measures are desirable and may so regulate. As an alternative we might either (1) ban the importation or taking of all endangered species or (2) leave regulation of all endangered species to the discretion of the Secretary. Commercialization is not the only purpose for which endangered species might be imported. Frequently non-commercial purposes need not be banned--in fact strict restriction could sometimes be harmful to the species. For example, allowing importation of individual trophies can provide for economic incentives for countries to manage the species and its habitat. On the other hand, Secretarial discretion for all endangered species could leave the Secretary subject to pressures to grant individual exceptions for importation of species threatened with extinction.
Alternative 2: The proposed legislation renews authority for the Secretary to acquire lands under the Land and Water Conservation Fund without a ceiling. Alternatives are to replace the old ceiling with a new ceiling or to take no action at all on this measure. Land acquisition is one of the key measures available to assist in restoration of endangered species. Since the inception of the program, land costs have accelerated considerably, and the old ceilings threatened to limit needed acquisitions.
